components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Eq. (7), Appendix A
components.condition: Fixed-time NQC matching algebra only, using caller-supplied smooth functions and exact polynomial samples. A pinned-binary diagnostic of fitted coefficients at 0.125 M requested output finds 0.16–0.34% differences on an aligned row and 0.36–1.55% on an antialigned row; each fit uses its own trajectory and pre-NQC mode. Replacing printed targets with pinned source full-precision targets on the native matrices shifts coefficients by at most 1.1% and 6.0% of those respective public gaps in absolute magnitude, so target rounding is not the main cause on these native inputs. Replacing only the native local phase-basis matrix with its full-series natural-cubic counterpart slightly increases the phase-coefficient distance on both rows. The pinned wheel's GSL natural-cubic evaluator matches native full-series phase-basis derivatives on the exact native samples, and source-target GSL matching on those samples also fails to close the public coefficient gap. The public modes API returns a waveform with ringdown attached at its amplitude maximum, which is within one output sample of NQC matching for both strong-spin rows; it cannot reveal the unmodified spline samples across matching. At fixed orbital frequencies the same-output native/public radius and radial momentum differ by at most 4.0 and 49.6 ppm. With fixed native restart and 0.015625 M high-rate step, native coefficients are identical across four requested output steps from 0.125 to 0.015625 M, but pinned public coefficients vary by up to 0.27% and 1.69% on the two rows; still finer public output alone changes some coefficients by up to 1.52% and 2.98%. Fine-output public modes cannot supply the centered inputs of the frozen 0.125 M fit. Same-input compiled NQC parity, historical peak selection, trajectory differentiation and interpolation, branch behavior, and full-generator convergence remain unverified.

components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Sec. II.C and Appendix B; Berti et al. (2006), Appendix E
components.blocker: Bohé et al. specify interpolation of Berti's numerical results, not Berti's approximate analytic fit. An explicit pinned-binary gate finds native Torch/JAX QNM errors below 6e-7 at nine signed-spin points through the binary's j=0.9996 limit. The historical knots and interpolation rule are not identified; the native frontends clamp at |j|=0.9999 even though the raw Torch spline reaches 0.99999. Qualify the native replacement across the supported domain and through whole-waveform evidence.
